_doc: Entries left out of the coverage matrix denominator. Every exclusion carries a written reason, and the report lists them. A rule applies to all entries the data packages flag that way; an item names one entry. Nothing is excluded because it fails.

rules.reason: Marked deprecated by @mdn/browser-compat-data: browsers keep it only for old pages and new pages should not use it.
Marked obsolete by mdn-data: removed from the standard.
Marked nonstandard by mdn-data: a vendor-only name (mostly -webkit-, -moz- and -ms- prefixes) that is not part of what CSS defines.
Not on a standards track in @mdn/browser-compat-data: a single vendor's experiment that no standard defines.
A compatibility note in @mdn/browser-compat-data about how the element behaves, such as an implied rel or a parser rule, not an attribute anyone can write.
An attribute of an element that is itself excluded, so the element's reason covers it: a node cannot be that element.

html-element.html: The document shell: the published route and its Next.js layout own it, and a node always sits inside body.
html-element.head: The document shell: the published route owns it. Head content beyond the search metadata is plan gap 5 (page-level items), not an element-level question.
html-element.body: The document shell: the published route owns it, and a node always sits inside it.
html-element.title: Page-level: the page's metadata (PageMetadataModel) writes it, a node cannot.
html-element.meta: Page-level: outside the component tree by design, and blocked in nodes (blockedNodes.ts). See the security finding in the complete primitives plan.
html-element.base: Page-level and blocked in nodes (blockedNodes.ts): it would rewrite every link on the page.
html-element.link: Page-level and blocked in nodes (blockedNodes.ts): an external stylesheet is the same risk as a script. The hosted fonts have their own path.
html-element.script: Blocked in nodes on purpose (blockedNodes.ts). The designed replacement is the custom code primitive, an open decision in the plan, so it is not a coverage gap until that is decided.
html-element.style: Blocked in nodes on purpose (blockedNodes.ts). What a style element would add is measured directly by the selector and at-rule rows.

css-selector.Pseudo-classes: A category heading in mdn-data, not a selector. Each pseudo-class has its own row.
css-selector.Pseudo-elements: A category heading in mdn-data, not a selector. Each pseudo-element has its own row.
css-selector.Namespace separator: Only meaningful with @namespace, itself excluded, and published pages are HTML.

css-at-rule.@charset: Not authored: the published page is served as UTF-8 by the app and its stylesheet is inline.
css-at-rule.@import: Blocked on purpose: responsiveCss.ts drops it as an import-capable value. A stored page must not load foreign stylesheets.
css-at-rule.@namespace: For XML documents; published pages are HTML.

svg-element.script: Blocked in nodes on purpose (blockedNodes.ts matches the tag in any namespace), for the same reason as the HTML script element.
svg-element.style: Blocked in nodes on purpose (blockedNodes.ts matches the tag in any namespace). The selector and at-rule rows measure what a style element would add.

svg-attribute.view.svgView: A fragment identifier syntax for URLs, listed under the view element, not an attribute.

css-value.<frequency>: No CSS property takes a frequency in any browser (it comes from aural CSS), so no sample can be proven valid.
css-value.<frequency-percentage>: No CSS property takes a frequency in any browser, so no sample can be proven valid.
css-value.<time-percentage>: Defined for the grammar of future properties: no CSS property takes it yet, so no sample can be proven valid.
css-value.Hz: No CSS property takes a frequency in any browser, so no sample can be proven valid.
css-value.kHz: No CSS property takes a frequency in any browser, so no sample can be proven valid.
css-value.layer(): Only valid inside @import, which is blocked on purpose. Not a value of any property.
css-value.cross-fade(): Not implemented in Chromium, the browser this harness proves samples in, so no sample can be proven valid. The browser probe fails when that changes.
css-value.element(): Not implemented in Chromium, the browser this harness proves samples in, so no sample can be proven valid. The browser probe fails when that changes.

css-value.target-counter(): Not implemented in Chromium, the browser this harness proves samples in, so no sample can be proven valid. The browser probe fails when that changes.
css-value.target-counters(): Not implemented in Chromium, the browser this harness proves samples in, so no sample can be proven valid. The browser probe fails when that changes.

css-value.paint(): Chromium refuses it on the probe's page, which registers no paint worklet, so no sample can be proven valid. The browser probe fails when that changes.
